layout.b_byte_of_element: p*64 + (j*E + e)*size, with k = p*E + e
layout.element_e_at_byte: e*size inside the word, little-endian: element 0 is the LOW bits
layout.a_word_index_equals_b_line_index: both are the k-group, k = word*E + e

stream_order.warning: THE STREAM IS NOT THE SAME IN ALL THREE TYPES. fp32 and fp16 run on txfma; int8 runs on TIMA and does all sixteen B columns in one micro-op, so it has no h half-pass loop. Corrected Sat 31 Oct 2026 after verification: the first version of this file asserted the txfma stream for all three types, which the measured 318 cycles an op refutes.

fp32.loops: for k in 0..15: for i in 0..15: for h in 0,1
fp32.a_changes_every: 2 micro-ops, walking down A's word-column k
fp32.b_changes_every: 1 micro-op, alternating columns l and l+8 of the same B line, 16 times per k-group

stream_order.fp16: identical to fp32 (the same txfma unit, vpu_tensorfma.v:622); only E and K differ

int8.loops: for p in 0..15: for i in 0..15        (NO h loop)
int8.a_operand: Aword[i][p], broadcast to all 16 column slots
int8.b_operand: the whole line Bword[p][0..15], one word per column slot
int8.a_changes_every: 1 micro-op, walking down A's word-column p — the opposite of fp32
int8.b_changes_every: 16 micro-ops: the line is held for its whole k-group, so only the 16 line boundaries cost anything on the B side
int8.why: fma_exec_last_b_col is forced true by req_int8 (vpu_tensorfma.v:412) and fma_exec_b_col_next never advances (:717-718, '// First go to next B col block (for INT8, we do all B cols at once)'), so there is one micro-op per (p, i), not two. 256 micro-ops fit the measured 318 cycles an op; 512 at one a cycle cannot. int8 also runs on a different unit: clock_en_txfma = enabled_int & ~req_int8, clock_en_tima = enabled_int & req_int8 (:157-166), and fma_en is clocked only when ~req_int8 (:626-628).
int8.provisional: the 256 micro-ops and the 16-column bus follow from the loop RTL and the 318 cycles, but they are a RECONSTRUCTION, not a cycle-accurate simulation: int8 has no bench. The GATED fractions do not depend on it (they depend only on the (A word, B column-pair) set and the gate rule); the int8 hamming and bus_bits_per_op figures do, and are marked provisional per kind.

zero_gating.rule: ex_tensor_zero_mask = A_zero | (tenB_zero[raddr] & tenB_zero[raddr|1]); it clears ex_txfma_valid (fp32/fp16) or ex_tima_valid (int8), and only for VPU_FCMD_MADD
zero_gating.a_side: one flag on the full 32-bit A word, broadcast to all 8 gate bits: an A word of zero gates the whole micro-op
zero_gating.b_side: one gate bit per lane, on a 32-bit slice of a TenB row
zero_gating.test_against_gate: there is ONE zero test and it is 32 bits wide in every type, taken when the tensor operand register is written (vpu_ctrl.v:1229-1234) — so the word-zero RATE is p^E for element sparsity p. What differs is how many of those tests a GATE DECISION needs: one in fp32 and fp16, and in int8 two, ANDed. Do not quote the word-zero rate as the gated rate in int8: it is p^4 against p^8.

fp32.rule: the lane's own 32-bit B word must be zero

fp16.rule: BOTH halves of the lane's 32-bit B word must be zero

int8.rule: ALL EIGHT bytes of the column PAIR (l, l+8) must be zero — the mask ANDs the two TenB rows of the B line, and one gate bit covers both column slots
int8.why: s1_tima_tenb_raddr = {fma_exec_b_rd_ptr, 1'b0} (vpu_tensorfma.v:863), so raddr and raddr|1 are the two halves of one 64-byte B line (a TenB row is VPU_DATA_SZ = 8*32 = 256 b = 8 words); ex_tensorb_zero_mask_tima1[l] is only forced to 1 when ~ex_tima_mask[l][1], and ex_tima_mask[l][t] = ex_fma_mask[(l>>1)+(t<<2)] = 1 for every (l, t) at cols_b = 3 (vpu_tensorfma.v:654-663, 899), so both TIMAs are live and the AND is real. For fp32 and fp16 ex_tima_valid_unqual is 0, both terms address ex_ra2_ten, and the AND is a no-op — which is why the 32-bit rule is right for those two types only.
int8.corrected: Sat 31 Oct 2026: the first version of this file said ALL FOUR bytes.
int8.which_pair: the pair is columns (l, l+8), because ex_tensor_zero_mask_ext[l][t] uses the SAME bit l for both TIMAs while tima0 reads TenB row raddr (words 0-7 = columns 0-7) and tima1 row raddr|1 (words 8-15 = columns 8-15); the enable mapping ex_tima_mask[l][t] = ex_fma_mask[(l>>1)+(t<<2)] puts unit (l, t) on column 2*((l>>1)+4t) + (l&1), which is column l at t=0 and column l+8 at t=1 — the same answer twice. E79 amendment A4 instead states the grouping as the eight CONTIGUOUS bytes of columns (2l, 2l+1). Both are 'eight bytes must be zero', so every kind here also carries stats.gated_lane_frac_alt_grouping under A4's reading: the two agree to within a per-tile band and no claim depends on which is right. Open for Q130(b).

zero_gating.bench_rule_is_fp32_only: rtl-sim/fma_toggle/tb.sv:56 lane_valid[l] = uop_valid & (uop_mul | ((uop_a != 32'b0) & (uop_b[l] != 32'b0))) states the fp32/fp16 rule; the bench has no int8 path
zero_gating.first_op_not_gated: the first op of a launch is a multiply pass (MUL) and is never gated; in int8 the gate also needs ex_tima_ren3 && ~ex_tima_last_pass (vpu_ctrl.v:827)

fp16_two_term_rule.rule: the two-term update c += a1*b1 + a2*b2 happens only when all four of a1, a2, b1, b2 are nonzero, except on the first op (MUL), which always multiplies
fp16_two_term_rule.note: this is ARITHMETIC (what lands in C) and is NOT the zero gate: a word with one nonzero half is not gated, but its update is dropped

hamming_convention.transitions: cyclic over the micro-ops of one op (micro-op t against t+1, the last against the next op's first): 512 in fp32 and fp16, 256 in int8. The convention of tools/claims-v3/hl/make_hl.py fma_flips
hamming_convention.bus_bits_per_op: slots*dA + sum over the slots of dB, summed over the transitions, with slots = 8 for fp32 and fp16 and 16 for int8
hamming_convention.A_BROADCAST_IS_A_CONVENTION: counting the one broadcast A word once per column slot is inherited from tb.sv (LANES * $countones(uop_a ^ pa)) and make_hl.py fma_flips. It is NOT a measurement. The same multiplier sits on both sides, so an A-against-B comparison of bus_bits_per_op is exactly a comparison of mean dA against mean dB and the broadcast contributes nothing to the ratio. Physically, if the broadcast word travels one net with fanout rather than one register per lane, this convention overcounts the A side: E70 already measured shared-wire carry-over at 1.246. E78 must validate the A-side weight before any of this is quoted as energy.

replay_in_rtl.fp32: exact: that is the unit and the stream the bench implements
replay_in_rtl.fp16: the right OPERAND WORDS, the right stream and the right gate, but fp32 arithmetic inside the unit: quote its bus and gate counts, not its multiplier-tree counts
replay_in_rtl.int8: DO NOT replay an int8 tile for gate or bus counts. The bench is txfma with the h half-pass loop and the 32-bit-word gate; int8 on the card runs on TIMA with 256 micro-ops, 16 column slots and a 64-bit column-pair gate. The bench would report the operand words correctly and everything derived from the stream or the gate wrongly. (Corrected Sat 31 Oct 2026: the first version of this file said int8 replays correctly.)

int8.note: value_sort_naive sorts each A word-column and each B line ascending in place and knows nothing about the stream; value_sort_pair_aware deals each sorted B line into the (l, l+8) pairs, so it already uses half of the stream fact. Both hold the base kind's operand multiset exactly.
